newsitem.title: USA: CMI says gross margins pressure persists.
newsitem.headline: CMI says gross margins pressure persists.

text.p: CMI Corp, a maker of automatic road building equipment said it is still fighting against gross margin pressures and the lack of basic deals.
Commenting on the company's second quarter results, Jim Holland, the chief financial officer of CMI said, "Business is strong. However, we are still suffering from gross margin pressure."

"We told investors earlier this year that we expected some low- margin orders to continue being filled into the second quarter and that has indeed happened. Additionally, we have had a continuation of fewer 'bread- and-butter' deals and more specialized equipment orders, along with the transaction discounting that was required to remain competitive," Holland added.

The company also said it was hurt by higher than normal costs at its Oklahoma City operations. Holland explained in a statement, "Our cost of revenues, and specifically the cost of labor, has remained higher than normal as we continue the changes in our very large Oklahoma City plant operations to make manufacturing more productive and our equipment more efficient."

However, Holland also pointed out a potential bright spot. "The latter factor should have a steadily diminishing affect, therefore, there is some reason to believe we can see a positive result in gross margin beginning during the second half of the year."
